segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello there and welcome to Real Easy English, the podcast where we have real conversations

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: in easy English to help you learn. I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And I'm Beth. Remember, you can read along with this episode on our website,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: How's your week going, Beth?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah, very good, thank you. Neil, how are you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm pretty good, thank you. What are we talking about today?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, today we are talking about our hometowns. That is the places that we are from.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK, so where are you from, Beth?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I am from Cumbria, but specifically I grew up in a very small, quiet village, almost in the middle of nowhere.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: What about you? Where did you grow up?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well I am originally from Portsmouth which is a city on the south coast of England but I moved around quite a lot Not really lived in Portsmouth much

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Ah, OK. So, Neil, you lived in a lot of places when you were younger,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: but where would you say that you grew up? So, where did you live mostly when you were a child?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, I lived in Canada from the age of four until ten, so I grew up a lot in Canada.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But also then we moved back to England and I did the rest of my growing up in the south of England.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Really interesting. So when you lived in Canada, what was your hometown like? What kind of place was it?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, it was a suburb, so it was quite quiet, but it was quite close to a big city, Toronto.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So you could go to the big city, but mostly when I was that age, I just stayed in my neighbourhood,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: which was quite quiet and boring.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah I suppose I didn live in a suburb I lived in a village but it was outside of a city And that city was quite busy

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So lots of people, but because I didn't spend loads of time there unless I went shopping,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: where I grew up was just quite quiet and small, maybe even boring, to be honest.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So Beth, do you miss your hometown?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I really liked living in the countryside.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: There were loads of fields around and it was really easy to just have a nice walk and not see anybody.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Whereas where I live now, there's lots of houses and lots of people.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So it's quite different.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Do you miss growing up in Canada?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Would you consider moving back there?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I don't know.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: It's a long time ago.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I had a nice time as a child.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: There was lots of freedom and I could go and play in the woods and in fields with my friends.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So that was really good fun And there was loads of snow in the winter which was brilliant because we always had a white Christmas

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Let's recap the vocabulary we heard during the conversation. We had grew up in, lived

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: somewhere when you were a child.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And we heard lots of adjectives to describe places, like busy, meaning lots of activity

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: and people.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Quiet. Not much noise or activity. For example, Beth, your village was quiet. There was not much happening there.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And boring. Not interesting.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Thanks for listening to Real Easy English. Find more programmes to help you with your English on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Next time, we'll talk about technology.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: See you then!

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Goodbye!

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Thank you.
